_source.money_model: All figures are millions of USD, in the year of the deal. The fair range is DERIVED from per_user x users_m rather than stored, so the two can never disagree.

brief.headline: A company with no revenue. How do you put a price on it?
brief.body: The world's biggest social network wants to buy a two-year-old photo-sharing app. It has 13 staff, about 30 million users and no revenue. Another tech company is also interested.
brief.client_line: The client is the buyer. You are advising them on what to pay.
brief.mood_line: Mobile is exploding. Two large platforms are racing to own the photo layer, and neither wants the other to get there first.

terminal.lede: Every page is fictional in name but based on real, dated facts.

pages.label: Company
pages.title: Prism
pages.body: A photo-sharing app. Founded 2010. Thirteen staff. About thirty million users. No revenue, and no plan for any this year.

pages.label: News · 2012
pages.title: In the news
pages.body: Dated items only. Nothing after the deal date appears anywhere in this terminal.

items.text: The app's Android version launched. Over a million downloads on day one.
Two large platforms have looked at the company, according to people familiar with the talks.
The app passes thirty million registered users.
A year-end list names it the app of the year.

pages.label: Industry
pages.title: How this sector works
pages.body: Mobile photo sharing is the fastest-growing part of social. Users are moving from desktop to phones faster than the big platforms can follow.

items.text: A large platform can build a photo feature in a quarter.
It cannot easily build the habit. That is what is scarce.
Switching costs for users are close to zero, so scale is the only moat.

pages.label: Comparables
pages.title: Three earlier app deals
pages.body: Similar companies, or similar deals, with simple numbers. Price per user has risen every year.

pages.label: Filings
pages.title: What the company has filed
pages.body: Prism is a private company. It files no accounts and publishes no financials.

items.text: There are no audited accounts to read.
The only numbers available are the ones the company chooses to share.

task.prompt: Which number shows what Prism is worth?
task.hint: Revenue and profit are zero. Pick the number that matters most to the buyer.
task.wrong_metric_explanation: Revenue and profit are zero because there is nothing to sell yet. The buyer is not paying for what the company earns today — it is paying for the users it would otherwise have to win one at a time. Try another number.
task.per_user_label: Price per user in earlier app deals
task.range_note: Thirty million users at $18 to $50 each.
task.right_call: Go, at a price inside a sensible range. Go with a stay bonus for the team also counts.

call.hint: Pick one. You can review before it locks.

choices.label: Go
choices.blurb: Buy at the agreed price and terms.

choices.label: Walk away
choices.blurb: Advise the client not to buy.

call.protection_note: Each tool is explained in one line.

protections.label: Lower price
protections.blurb: Pay less than the asking price.

protections.label: Money held back
protections.blurb: Part of the price is released later, once conditions are met.

protections.label: Seller guarantee
protections.blurb: The seller pays out if something they told you turns out to be untrue.

protections.label: Earnout
protections.blurb: Part of the price is paid later, only if targets are hit.

protections.label: Stay bonus for team
protections.blurb: Money for the staff, paid only if they stay.

call.reason_label: Say in one line why the board should agree

reasons.text: Growth this fast would take the client years to build in-house.
The price sits inside the range the app deals support.
The client's balance sheet can absorb the price.
The target is small enough to absorb quickly.

call.note_label: Optional sentence, saved for the report

receipt.line: A deal receipt appears. No outcome yet.
receipt.detail: The Deal Book opens the next deal. What really happened is revealed at the Truth.

companion.brief: Read the brief before you look at any number.
companion.research: Save what you find. Facts and risks, not impressions.
companion.task: No revenue does not mean no value. What does the buyer get that it cannot build fast?
companion.call: Your price is inside your range. Say in one line why the board should agree.
companion.receipt: That is your call on the record. We find out at the Truth.
